messages:
Incident Bot: P1 alert triggered: synthetic /health checks spike in eu-west after greenswap rollout. Error rate -> 18% 502/504s, latency p95 up 3x. Links: https://telemetry/redwood/alert/2109876543 :pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345
Eric (oncall): acked. picking this up. looking at traces now. any quick wins before full rollback?
Alice: seeing a lot of 502s from model-proxy in eu-west-green nodes. recent deploy looked like green got 60% traffic for canary.
Raj: confirmed. router weights report shows eu-west: blue=40 green=60. That flip was supposed to be gradual. Noticed mismatch between router config and LB targets.
Maria: customer impact: support queue shows ~12 Dedicated tenant alerts in EU with generation failures. No data exfil reported.
Sam (SRE): if green backend is failing we should hit the feature-flag kill switch then remove green from LB. Kill switch name is rollout_green_2026. Runbook: https://wiki/redwood/rollouts/runbook#kill-switch
Eric (oncall): running kill switch now (manual toggle).
Eric (oncall): command: ```bash
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/flags/rollout_green_2026/toggle -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN" -d '{"state":"off"}'
```
Incident Bot: Feature flag rollout_green_2026 toggled -> off by Eric (oncall) at 2109876612.
Alice: traffic shifted but still see ~6% errors. TTL/cached clients likely still hitting green origin IPs.
Sam (SRE): correct — DNS TTLs and some persistent LB connections. Next step: remove green backend from LB pool in eu-west. Do we have permission to run remove-target?
Raj: I can run it. Command: ```bash
lbctl remove-target --region eu-west --pool green --reason "emergency rollback"
```
Raj: executed remove-target at 2109876701. Health checks show green nodes draining.
Maria: support update draft: "We experienced a partial degradation for EU customers during a routine greenswap. We reverted the rollout and removed the affected backend. Services are recovering; some requests may have retried and succeeded. We're following up with affected customers."
Eric (oncall): metrics: error rate dropped from 18% -> 1.2% in last 3 mins. Latency back to baseline.
Alice: logs show root cause appears to be a protobuf size regression in model-proxy 2.8.1 on green pool only (packaging bug).
Sam (SRE): noted for postmortem. Owner?
Raj: I'll lead the postmortem and coordinate with eng-runtime to revert the model-proxy packaging. Tagging @eng-runtime.
Maria: customer comms: I'll send the support note + list of affected tenants. Also notify AE for high-touch customers.
Eric (oncall): handing off active incident monitoring to Sam for the next 60m. If anything spikes, page me.
Sam (SRE): taking over. Will keep watch for 60m then hand to Raj for long-term remediate. Setting incident channel to #incidents/2109876543 and updating status to "stabilized - rollback".
Incident Bot: Incident P1 updated: stabilized -> mitigated. Postmortem owner: Raj. Follow-ups: rollback timeline, packaging fix, add rollout pre-check for protobuf size.
Alice: quick note — please block any auto-rollouts for model-proxy 2.8.x until fix shipped.
Raj: agreed. adding block to release config.
Maria: closing support loop: pinging AEs and sending initial incident summary.
Sam (SRE): thanks everyone. I'll keep a 1hr watch and then close the thread when safe. :white_check_mark:
